bindings.title: A whole-word candidate binds one botanical part class
Modal obligation is distinct from descriptive action

findings.IDEA000027: Part-name versus generic material is not identified by simple part co-occurrence: a generic material can concentrate on the same part. Text may instruct use of an undrawn part. Independent opportunity/exhaustiveness assumptions and rival predictions are missing. IDEA15 already proposes part concentration with held folios and independently named parts;27narrows the named class but has no newly established independent endpoint. Preserve related distinct proposals, do not assert scientific novelty or exact identity.
findings.IDEA000028: Plain action meaning does not entail absence of contextual modality. A separate neighboring operator or construction can supply obligation/prohibition/condition. Independent action, polarity and scope endpoints must be supplied without translating the target by the proposed meaning. External-language modal annotation is not automatically manuscript gold. GDT238 is misrouted in the authored proposal: its modal baseline means the most frequent geometric class, not linguistic obligation. Its visible attachment/proximity mode is not a predecessor test of must/may/not.
findings.IDEA000029: A stable lexical core can occur in different genre-specific argument/field roles. Thus a genre interaction is not a contrast against portable meaning unless the rival explicitly predicts role invariance. Independently identified genres and roles are missing; record/page labels alone do not supply them. A null result also needs adequacy and an explicit effect definition before rejecting the compound interaction claim.
